headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: oh-my-openagent can ingest project files and external APIs while dagster is a non-writing orchestrator, creating unsafe default trust boundaries.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent reads project files and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so attacker-controlled content in shared files can influence its prompts; dagster itself has no shared channel or file I/O, so the pathway is one-way and not provably blocked. The interaction is inferred from B’s file surfaces and A’s lack of isolation, not directly documented.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent is pointed at a workspace containing untrusted AGENTS.md or README.md content
IF runtime-injected MCPs or hooks pass file content into model prompts
mitigations: Restrict oh-my-openagent to a clean workspace
Disable or review runtime-injected MCPs and hooks
Mark untrusted repo files as non-authoritative in prompts
Use a separate read-only clone for analysis
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: oh-my-openagent has broad network egress and touches project code, session history, and provider auth data; dagster is docs-only here and does not itself expose data, but if dagster-managed artifacts are opened by B, B can transmit them to third-party APIs. The blast radius includes code and auth material, so the default pair is dangerous.
conditions: IF dagster outputs contain secrets, credentials, or proprietary code
IF oh-my-openagent sends those artifacts to external services such as PostHog, Exa, or provider APIs
mitigations: Exclude secrets from dagster outputs
Disable external API calls in oh-my-openagent
Use a redacted workspace for shared artifacts
Rotate any exposed provider credentials
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists per data class

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dagster cannot write or modify git state, while oh-my-openagent can spawn subprocesses and has broad egress; there is no direct same-directory write conflict from A, but B can still contend over shared files and runtime state if both are pointed at the same installation or workspace. Uncertainty about the exact shared mutable surface pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same writable workspace or installation
IF oh-my-openagent subprocesses modify files that dagster also reads or schedules
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Run only one writer per repository
Disable subprocess-based mutators in oh-my-openagent
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can act on project code and external lookups, so if dagster-produced outputs are treated as authoritative inputs, B may propagate errors into downstream actions. Dagster itself is not an action-taking agent here, but the pair still forms a default trust chain from A’s artifacts into B’s outputs without a verification step.
conditions: IF dagster-generated artifacts are consumed by oh-my-openagent without validation
IF oh-my-openagent uses those artifacts to draft messages, edits, or tool calls
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions
Add schema validation for dagster outputs
Annotate generated artifacts as untrusted
Limit oh-my-openagent to read-only summarization
requires-engineering: insert verification gates before action tools

E_compliance.rationale: oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts, session history, and project code, while dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes; the main compliance issue is B’s broader retention and telemetry surface if regulated data from A’s workflows is introduced. Because only B has explicit data-handling surfaces, A is cited only to show the upstream source is absent here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into oh-my-openagent session history or provider auth prompts
IF retention or telemetry settings are left at defaults while such data is present
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of session history
Disable telemetry where possible
Review retention settings before use
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
